title: What the page assumes until you change it
status: Set by Claude at the owner's request (30-09-2026: work everything out from this year's figures and sales growth, and assume the rest). Chosen to be reasonable and on the careful side for a lender; not checked against a published source. Every one is shown on the page and can be changed.

assumptions.why: How chartered accountants and banks usually work it for term loans (docs/DSCR-RESEARCH.md)
The commonly quoted examples (benchmarks in dscr.json); each lender sets its own
The rate for a firm or LLP, and the top rate for an individual with cess: on the careful side, since more tax gives a lower DSCR. Say who the borrower is to work out the tax for that borrower

assumptions.shown: The new regime's slab rates, on the business's profit as the only income
assumptions.why: Other income would put the profit in higher slabs, and the old regime (with deductions) is not offered: type a rate if either applies

assumptions.shown: As this year: profit before interest, depreciation and tax grows with sales
assumptions.why: The only growth asked for is in sales

assumptions.what: Extra income from the new asset
assumptions.why: Leaving it out errs low. Add it if the asset adds to profit, from the month it starts running
Depreciation on the asset the loan buys is left out; it lowers tax, so leaving it out errs low

assumptions.shown: As this year, every year, on top of this loan's interest
assumptions.why: Working-capital limits are taken as unchanged
Change it if EMIs are paid on other loans: all of a proprietor's, business and personal; a firm's, LLP's or company's own loans only

assumptions.what: Other non-cash charges and lease rentals
The first year of the figures
assumptions.shown: The year the loan is first drawn
assumptions.why: The business is running: it has this year's figures
